data.title: Gold's slide deepens as AI rout, rate hike bets hurt bullion
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold slips for fifth session, hits lowest since September 2025
  • Markets may soon see gold and silver prices bottom - analyst
  • Gold, silver, platinum, palladium head for second straight weekly decline

By Anjana Anil and Vishak Mathew

Gold's bearish spell continued on Friday as it floundered to a 14-month low and headed for its worst week in eight months, amid pressure from a hawkish interest rate outlook and an AI-linked stocks selloff.

Spot gold fell 2.5% to $3,530.47 per ounce by 12:20 p.m. ET (1720 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,513.54 earlier in the session.

Bullion has shed about 9.2% so far this week, the most since the week ended March 20.

US gold futures for December delivery dropped 4.2% to $3,531.30 per ounce.

"The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses," said David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures.

Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI trade, with US futures dropping and Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020.

"Higher interest rates, stronger dollar, the prospects for ongoing high inflation, which prompts the Fed to continue to raise interest rates — all of those factors that we have been seeing — negatively affect gold," Meger said.

Gold's fall has been accentuated by comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers that echoed hawkish tones in the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) October meeting. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson flagged inflation risks that could warrant another interest-rate increase, reinforcing expectations that US borrowing costs will rise further.

Markets see a 96% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"Prices in the next few sessions could still drop a lot more. But from a time perspective, it's very likely that we're going to see a bottom in the gold and silver markets sooner rather than later," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.

Spot silver fell 3.6% to $41.23 per ounce, around 66% below its record high of $121.64 hit in January.

Platinum dropped 2.6% to $1,308.75, and palladium slid 2.1% to $890.25. All precious metals are poised for their second straight weekly declines.

Further update on High Court Proceedings brought by PIFSS

Following a further hearing held this week[1], the High Court has ordered two Man Group subsidiaries to make an aggregate payment of approximately $107 million to the Kuwaiti Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS). This sum reflects the $155 million which the judgment indicated PIFSS was entitled to recover, taking into account deductions in relation to co-defendant settlements.

The payment will be made this month and will be satisfied from existing resources.

Considering the complexity of the claim, the High Court has not yet passed judgment on certain other disputed matters that will affect Man Group’s total financial liability, including interest if applicable, and costs. Man Group intends to make a further announcement once the High Court hands down judgment on these matters which the Court has indicated may not happen until early 2027.

Man Group continues to disagree with the judgment in respect of both liability and quantum and is considering all legal options, including the option to appeal.

data.title: Tencent Stocks Slip 1.26% as Sixfold Capex Jump Pushes Cash Flow Negative
data.description:
Tencent Holdings (TCEHY) slipped 1.26% to HK$344 at the November 20 regular-session close in Hong Kong, extending a slide that took the shares to their lowest level since May 2024 the day before. The trigger was a third-quarter report that missed on revenue and showed AI spending racing ahead of returns.

Revenue rose 8% to RMB207.3 billion, short of the roughly RMB210.8 billion LSEG consensus. Marketing services grew 19% and cloud revenue climbed 35%. But non-IFRS operating profit fell 6% to RMB68.1 billion, and the margin shrank to 33% from 38%. Capital expenditure jumped to RMB81.4 billion from RMB13.0 billion a year earlier, and free cash flow was negative RMB69.1 billion. Excluding compute prepayments, free cash flow would have been a positive RMB16.9 billion. Tencent still holds RMB525.7 billion in cash and bought back about HK$7.0 billion of shares in the quarter.

Capex now equals about 39% of quarterly revenue. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 93/100, built on strong profitability and decent momentum, with the balance sheet the softer spot as spending ramps. GF Value is HK$560.37, a 38.6% discount to the close, which GuruFocus rates significantly undervalued. The discount is real, but it rests on margins Tencent has just chosen to sacrifice. The next test is whether cloud and WorkBuddy revenue grows fast enough to turn compute prepayments back into positive cash flow.

data.title: Trump officials met privately with investors on Norfolk/Union Pacific deal - Bloomberg
data.description:
Trump officials met privately with a group of hedge fund investors who are betting on the outcome of Union Pacific's $72 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern .

The meeting included investors from several major hedge funds and multiple officials from Trump's administration, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. The funds that attended the meeting specialize in merger arbitrage.

Administration officials didn't share non-public information at the meeting, according to the report.

A White House official said in a statement to Bloomberg that a junior staffer, who no longer works at the White House, attended a lunch off the White House complex and that his attendance wasn’t authorized.

Union Pacific () and Norfolk Southern () filed a response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City's request that the Surface Transportation Board terminate review of the merger application for a transcontinental railroad.

The Dept. of Justice is expected to give its opinion on the deal by Dec. 3. The DOJ is likely to remain neutral on the rail combination, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report at the time.

The STB is expected to issue its final decision within 90 days of the record closing, targeting final approval and transaction completion by late summer 2027.

data.title: Govt Mulls Expanding Unified EV Charging Platform Beyond Five-State Pilot
data.description:
Expansion hinges on adding more charging operators and improving network reliability across the EV ecosystem

The government plans to expand the Unified Bharat e-Charge platform beyond its ongoing five-state pilot as more charging network operators join the system, according to the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Around 12 charging network operators are currently integrated with the platform, which allows electric vehicle (EV) users to find and access charging stations operated by different companies through a common interface.

The expansion will depend on the network achieving greater scale and reliability. The government has not announced a timeline for taking the platform beyond the pilot states. NPCI BHIM Services and Bharat Heavy Electricals (Bhel) developed the platform. The system is also being integrated with electric two-wheeler, three-wheeler and four-wheeler manufacturers, according to the ministry.

The Unified Bharat e-Charge platform is part of the government's broader effort to create a common digital layer for India's fragmented EV charging ecosystem. The Ministry of Heavy Industries had earlier outlined the platform as a system through which users could discover and access chargers operated by multiple charging point operators.

Charging Reliability Key

The wider rollout comes as the government focuses on improving the availability and reliability of public charging infrastructure. The operational guidelines for EV charging infrastructure under the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) scheme require charging points supported under the programme to be onboarded on the Unified Bharat e-Charge platform. The guidelines also require implementing agencies and charging point operators to maintain high charger uptime, with performance to be monitored through the national platform.

The government has allocated Rs 2,000 crore under PM E-Drive for public EV charging infrastructure. The scheme is intended to support charging deployment across cities and major transport corridors. The Ministry of Heavy Industries said in March that 8,932 EV chargers had been installed by oil marketing companies under the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME) II scheme as of 1 March 2026, while 6,645 of the sanctioned chargers were operational.

The government has also identified national highways as a priority for charging infrastructure, with freight and passenger vehicle corridors being considered for electrification. The expansion of Unified Bharat e-Charge will therefore mark a shift from building individual charging networks towards connecting them through a common platform. Its effectiveness will depend on the number of operators and chargers onboarded, as well as the reliability of the charging points available to users.

data.title: Wall Street sinks as the tech space remains under heavy pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were mostly lower on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year.

The blue-chip Dow was last +0.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -1.2%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite was last -2.3%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, six of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area.

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities.

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield dropped 11 basis points to 4.64%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield shifted down 10 basis points to 4.94%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield moved down 7 basis points to 5.33%.

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. advanced +6.5%, while shares of Sandisk dropped -13.8%.

data.title: Canadian dollar falls for third straight week as stock market selloff deepens
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar edged higher against its US counterpart on Friday but was still headed for a weekly decline, as a selloff in equity markets deepened globally, and following downbeat preliminary domestic retail sales data.

The loonie was trading 0.1% higher at 1.4325 per US dollar, or 69.81 US cents, after moving in a range of 1.4300 to 1.43465.

  • On Thursday, the currency touched its weakest intraday level since April 2025 at 1.43575. It was on track to decline 0.3% for the week, which would be its third straight weekly decline.

  • "CAD prospects remain somewhat mixed as investors balance USD and equity market volatility plus softer crude oil and commodities against BoC hawkishness and signs that the US and Canada may be closer to making progress on trade," Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret, FX strategists at Scotiabank, said in a note.

  • On Thursday, the Canadian minister responsible for trade with the US, Dominic LeBlanc, said Ottawa had made some progress in trade talks with Washington but not enough to sign a deal.

  • Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% in September on a monthly basis as sales picked up at gasoline stations and fuel vendors, but most of the increase was due to higher prices, while a preliminary estimate showed sales declining 1.5% in October.

  • "The run of weak Canadian data continues," Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates & macro strategist at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note. "The case for a follow up Bank of Canada rate hike in December is becoming increasingly challenging."

  • Investors see a roughly 50% chance the BoC raises interest rates next month after it hiked in October for the first time in three years. (0#CADIRPR)

  • The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, added to its weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East. US crude oil futures were trading 0.6% lower at $82.75 a barrel, while the US dollar gave back some recent gains against a basket of major currencies.

  • Canadian bond yields moved lower as US Treasuries benefited from safe-haven demand. The 10-year (CA10YT=RR) was down 10.6 basis points at 3.703%, its lowest level since November 12.

data.title: Nymex Overview: Crude, Refined Products Lower as Supply Concerns Weigh — OPIS
data.description:
Crude futures moved lower with oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and recovering Middle Eastern production continuing to weigh on prices despite lingering concerns over regional conflict.

Both major benchmarks were on track for a third consecutive weekly decline.

January ICE Brent crude was trading 74cts lower at $91.24/bbl on Friday, while the February contract was down 67cts at $88.77/bbl.

December West Texas Intermediate slipped 46cts to $82.75/bbl, with January WTI off 43cts at $82.01/bbl.

Refined product futures were also lower. December ULSD fell 2.05cts to $3.9309/gal, with the January contract down 0.9ct at $3.8524/gal.

The December RBOB contract was trading 1.42cts lower at $2.4809/gal, with January down 1.12cts at $2.4580/gal.

Macquarie Group said resilient flows through the Strait remain a central factor for energy markets, including liquefied natural gas. Continued shipments through the waterway, alongside the persistence of the Iran blockade, could maintain pressure on oil prices, although the potential for further escalation in the region remains a risk, analysts said.

Recent U.S. Energy Information Administration data also point to improving regional supply. Oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints increased 19% in the third quarter from the previous three months, while regional crude production reached 23.1 million b/d in October, its highest level since the conflict began. EIA expects recovering Middle Eastern production and exports to contribute to rising global inventories, with relatively flat near-term demand.

data.title: MasTec Pasted Despite Murphy Purchase
data.description:
MasTec, Inc. today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Murphy Corporation, one of the largest and most respected mechanical contractors in the United States.

Founded in 1907 and continuously family owned and operated for more than 119 years, Murphy has built a scaled, full-service platform providing mechanical, plumbing and process infrastructure solutions across mission-critical end markets. With approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals and national execution capabilities, Murphy serves a diversified portfolio of customers in aviation and defense, healthcare, pharmaceutical manufacturing, technology, food processing, refrigeration and advanced manufacturing, supported by industry-leading engineering, preconstruction and fabrication capabilities.

Murphy's experienced management team, led by CEO Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the Transaction.

In addition to its large-scale construction capabilities, Murphy maintains a substantial service and maintenance business providing recurring HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, controls and other mechanical services to mission-critical facilities as well as other market sectors.

MasTec believes this business is positioned for significant growth as Murphy expands its owner-direct relationships and supports the increasing number of data centers and other large-load facilities transitioning from construction into ongoing operation. This recurring service revenue complements Murphy’s project-based operations, strengthens customer relationships and enhances the resilience and visibility of its financial performance.

data.title: Tech Rout Deepens as Anthropic Stock Slides — WSJ
data.description:

The selloff in technology stocks is intensifying, dragging the S&P 500 and Dow industrials into correction territory.

The Nasdaq is sliding more than 3% as investors continue to pull money out of AI stocks, and Anthropic shares are down 11%, giving up a big chunk of their day-one gains.

The Dow, down about 175 points Friday, and the S&P 500, off about 1.8%, both were recently trading in correction territory, generally defined as 10% or more off a recent peak.

The S&P 500 is headed for its seventh down day in a row, which would be its longest losing streak since 2020. The Dow is down more than 6% for the week.

Investors also are watching whether Anthropic will slip below its IPO price of $83 a share. It was recently near $85.

The Claude maker's blockbuster debut Thursday did little to allay fears about the broader AI trade. "The AI buildout still needs vast amounts of funding just as financing costs are rising and signs of credit stress are emerging," said Swissquote's Ipek Ozkardeskaya. The prospect of tighter chip-export rules also is a worry, she added.

U.S. Treasurys are climbing, sending yields lower, as investors seek safe assets. The yield on the 10-year note has dipped below 5%. The dollar is hovering near a one-year high.

data.title: SpaceX-Owned Cursor Considers Dropping Chinese AI Models – A Look At Some Key Details
data.description:
Key points:
  • The report includes 12 policy recommendations aimed at reducing American dependence on Chinese AI technology.
  • Lawmakers recommended keeping China-developed AI models out of federal contract work and high-risk functions of critical infrastructure. 
  • SpaceX acquired Cursor in August in an all-stock transaction for about $60 billion to boost its AI business.

SpaceX’s (SPCX) AI coding platform Cursor is considering dropping Chinese-developed AI models amid geopolitical tensions, according to a congressional report released on Friday.

SPCX shares were down 6.6% at the time of writing.

Cursor Used Kimi K2.5 To Build Coding Model

The report, prepared by the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China, follows an investigation launched in April into American companies’ use of Chinese AI models and the potential security risks involved.

Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, which built its proprietary Composer 2 coding model using Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.5, informed lawmakers that it plans to explore moving away from Chinese-developed open-weight models.

“Anysphere informed the Committees that it plans to explore phasing out PRC-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk,” the report read.

SpaceX acquired Cursor in August in an all-stock transaction for about $60 billion to boost its AI business.

The investigation also examined Airbnb (ABNB), which uses Alibaba’s (BABA) Qwen models for customer support, and DoorDash (DASH), which has deployed multiple models developed in China.

Washington Pushes For Tighter AI Restrictions

The congressional report includes 12 policy recommendations aimed at reducing American dependence on Chinese AI technology. Among them, lawmakers recommended keeping China-developed AI models out of federal contract work and high-risk functions of critical infrastructure.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration is reportedly considering requiring American companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models. The proposal, described as a “name and shame” campaign, aims to discourage reliance on Chinese technology without introducing outright restrictions.

Chinese models have reportedly gained popularity among American businesses because of their lower costs and competitive performance, but Washington remains concerned about security risks and growing dependence on Chinese technology.

data.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says Claude Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Cohen

The day after Anthropic's historic IPO, a mathematician who works for the company went public with some history of his own.

He says he has discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis — the most famous unsolved problem in math.

Ever since the Riemann hypothesis was proposed in 1859, a proof of the iconic conjecture in number theory had eluded the brightest human minds. For 167 years, mathematicians tried to crack it. And for 167 years, they all failed. By the time it was selected as one of the seven notoriously difficult Millennium Prize Problems in 2000, it had become known as the field's holy grail. Even the smartest AI models hadn't been able to crack it.

But on Friday, Anthropic's Levent Alpöge revealed that he believes he's found the solution with the help of Claude.

If the proof checks out, it would count as the most remarkable accomplishment in the year of AI's extraordinary math progress. It would also be the second Millennium Prize Problem taken down by artificial intelligence, after an OpenAI model — and millions of dollars in computing power — managed to solve one in September. Humans alone have only solved one of these fiendishly difficult problems.

On his website, Alpöge posted the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows computers to verify it, line by line, and mathematicians immediately got to work trying to wrap their minds around the argument. He said the full argument is both "incredibly long" and "some massive unreadable travesty of 'slop,' " with the AI-written version clocking in at more than 250,000 pages.

The result was achieved late Sunday night into Monday, he said, days before Anthropic went public. Given the timing, which Alpöge called "horrible," he said he messaged CEO Dario Amodei to ask for permission to announce the solution. "The fact is that there was a constraint to respect," Alpöge wrote.

Anthropic didn't respond to a request for comment after he posted his findings on Friday morning, as the company's stock price dropped on its first full day of trading.

"I just could not live if I waited even longer," Alpöge wrote.

He added: "In a time of revolution in mathematics I hope the argument provides a glimpse towards the miracles that lie ahead, and shows us the joy and wonder we are about to find in the simplest things."

data.title: Buckle Marches on Quarterly Figures
data.description:
The Buckle, Inc. announced today that net income for the fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis).

Net sales for the quarter increased 2.6% to $329.2 million from net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Online sales decreased 1.4% to $52.2 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $53.0 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $48.7 million, or $0.97 per share ($0.96 per share on a diluted basis) for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Buckle is a specialty retailer focused on delivering exceptional service and style through unforgettable experiences. Offering a curated mix of high-quality, on-trend apparel, accessories, and footwear, Buckle is for those living the styled life.

Known as a denim destination, each store carries a wide selection of fits, styles, and finishes from leading denim brands, including the Company’s exclusive brand, BKE.

BKE shares spiked $2.71, or 6.5%, to $44.62.
